question: Compute a common, calibrated-probe iterative baseline from allowed measurements, independently of learned-model rank selection.
dependency_decision: Advances only standard visible-only baseline fitting while M3 completes. No learned-model training, family selection, query-target scoring, or official InverseBench access. This prospective baseline contract extends prior input-only preparation without changing its measurements or partitions.
task_order: Visible fraction outer loop; scans ordered by frame count except tied IC1/TP1 in stated order. This scheduling order never uses accuracy.
method: Pinned native LSQML, object-only; amplitude-Gaussian objective, default random minibatch sampling, fixed probe/positions/OPR. No new optimizer or tuned loss.
initialization: Constant object amplitude and numerical intensity scale from visible fluence only; no reference pixel access.
calibration: Supplied full-scan estimated probe and reconstructed canvas shape. Conditional calibration-assisted measurement prediction, not independent probe recovery or independent material-property validation.
data: Original detector values retained without rounding. Coordinates use already-confirmed parity offsets. LCLS excluded prospectively because its physical patch origin remains unconfirmed.
outputs: Complex128 object and float32 raw-unit query-intensity prediction at epochs100/300/1000; all query identities preserved. Full visible-only training trace and resource accounting. No query metrics.
primary: Epoch1000 is the fixed primary baseline. Epoch100/300 are computation/convergence diagnostics, never selected by query targets. No claim that1000 passes guarantees a global optimum.
future_strengthening: Any continuation or additional baseline requires a new prospective version and uses training-side convergence evidence only; preserve every completed1000-epoch output.
resources: Remote GPU0 with separate Python3.11.18/Torch2.6.0+cu124 runtime. Initially two independent processes, four CPU threads each. Concurrency may be1–4 for memory/throughput only; it cannot alter optimizer/batch/epochs.
timing: Concurrent task resource accounting, not an isolated algorithm speed benchmark.
failures: Stop new launches on a task failure, allow other active task to finish, preserve partial files and logs; inspect before any recovery.
